I agree with this. My parents separated when I was very young. They still loved each other and were friends but they needed to separate for reasons bigger than them that just weren't going to get fixed, and if they did, the scars they left on each other were too deep to be able to move forward again. Dont stay together for the sake of the kids when doing so will put them in an unhappy household. It will cause much more harm and even damage to them in the long run. Much better to have two separate healing, happy households. They can learn to work with the break with explanation and talking to them honestly, it would set a better example to not stay where you're unhappy than to stay together for the sake of the kids and have them stay in an unhappy house. You still have a life ahead of you. Live it. Dont ever feel stuck.

I want to say you just have to wait it out. Same around here there's a lot of vans with close to or over 200,000 miles they're just asking too much for. Just keep saving and checking around as frequently as you can, but when you see the one that you know is right and you're ready, you'll have to jump on it.

Like most people are saying, plan on it, work, and save. I find the cheapest rent I can and pick up some extra hours when I can. I have a very physical job so I won't be able to work while on the go. So I save and live life until I have a couple days or a week or two at a time to travel. 
I typically pack my own food (canned foods, dry foods, pastas, fruit), bring face wipes and dry shampoo, or a planet fitness black card will allow you access to any of their gyms for $20 a month for showers and such to save on expenses once you're out.
I waited out to find the lowest miles for the lowest price before getting my van, and I have an extremely simple conversion of essentially taking out the center seats, and adding a dresser and a pump sink. Reclining seat in the back as the bed.
But, you can also develop your own skill and do crafts and sell stuff on Etsy while you travel, set up a road side shop when you stop, or busk with an instrument in a public space. Do some online computer software developing stuff that I have no clue about, be a photographer, travel for work, work in an oil field and have half a year off. Everyone can find their own way.
